## What this notebook did not do

This is a pure-downstream analysis: it starts from called peaks, count matrices, BAM or bigWig. Where a step needed something this environment does not ship, the cell said so and continued — an existing message means that step did not run, not that it passed.

Next steps that belong elsewhere:

- **Raw reads to peaks** — alignment (bowtie2/BWA) and peak calling (MACS2) are the `nf-core/chipseq` wrapper, not notebook cells. CUT&Tag peak calling (SEACR) has no wrapper yet; pass its peaks in directly.
- **csaw on Apple Silicon** — bioconda has no osx-arm64 csaw build, so the window-based broad-mark route is a gap on darwin-arm64 (DiffBind still works). Run on linux-x64 / darwin-x64, or request a project environment.
- **IDR reproducibility** — the formal IDR test needs the `idr` pip package; this notebook reports peak-overlap fractions as a transparent proxy.
- **Motif analysis (HOMER/MEME), profileplyr, IDR** — these need packages or upstream tools the plugin omits; `chip_env_probe` lists them as gaps with a project-environment next step.
- **Gene symbols** — annotation needs a user org.db (annoDb) or GFF3 gene_name attributes; without one, peaks are annotated to gene ids, features and TSS distance.
attribution: The fragment explanations are an original distillation of the DiffBind, ChIPseeker and csaw Bioconductor vignettes (Artistic-2.0), the ENCODE ChIP-seq guidelines (Landt et al., Genome Res 2012, doi:10.1101/gr.136184.111) and the nf-core/chipseq documentation. No upstream notebook text, images or data are copied; the code runs in Phi's managed plugin:chip environment with no install cells and no hidden state between cells.

seed.comment: random seed, so normalization and tests repeat exactly

figures_dir.comment: directory for PNG figures; null disables saving

peak_paths.comment: explicit BED/narrowPeak/broadPeak files; empty uses data_path (file or directory)

count_path.comment: peak x sample count table; null uses data_path when it is a table

bam_paths.comment: explicit aligned BAM files; empty uses bam_dir or data_path

bam_dir.comment: directory of .bam files (with .bai indexes) for FRiP/counting

paired_end.comment: sequencing is paired-end; affects counting and csaw fragment handling

blacklist_path.comment: user ENCODE blacklist BED; overrides the inlined hg38/mm10 lists; null with no genome skips filtering

genome.comment: genome build (hg38 or mm10) selecting the inlined ENCODE v2 blacklist; other builds need blacklist_path

min_occupancy.comment: consensus peak must appear in at least this many samples

normalize_method.comment: libsize (CPM), rpkm (also divides by peak width), or none

contrast.comment: explicit contrast c(column, treated, control); empty tests all condition pairs

min_members.comment: minimum replicates per group for a DiffBind contrast

fdr_threshold.comment: FDR cutoff for calling a peak differential

lfc_threshold.comment: minimum absolute log2 fold change for a differential peak

top_n.comment: top differential peaks/regions printed and written

csaw_width.comment: csaw window width (bp); larger for broad marks

csaw_spacing.comment: csaw window spacing (bp); also the region-merge tolerance

csaw_filter.comment: csaw window filter: global (background) or control (input)

fragment_size.comment: single-end fragment extension (bp) for csaw; ignored when paired_end

gtf_path.comment: user GTF/GFF3 to build a TxDb (makeTxDbFromGFF) for annotation

txdb_path.comment: user prebuilt TxDb .sqlite (loadDb); takes precedence over gtf_path

org_db.comment: user org.db package name for gene symbols (e.g. org.Hs.eg.db); null reports gene ids

tss_upstream.comment: bp upstream of TSS for promoter definition and coverage profiles

tss_downstream.comment: bp downstream of TSS for promoter definition and coverage profiles

1.title: TF / narrow-mark ChIP — DiffBind + DESeq2
1.intro:
End-to-end downstream analysis of a transcription-factor or narrow-mark ChIP
experiment (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, CTCF). It starts from called peaks and aligned BAMs,
checks FRiP and replicate reproducibility, removes ENCODE blacklist artefacts, builds
a consensus peakset, counts reads, and tests differential binding with DiffBind +
DESeq2. Peaks are annotated to genomic features with a user-supplied GTF/GFF3.

Alignment and MACS2 peak calling belong to the nf-core/chipseq wrapper; this notebook
picks up at the peak files. The DiffBind sample sheet (SampleID, Condition, Replicate,
Peaks, PeakCaller, bamReads) drives the statistical design.

2.title: Broad mark — csaw window analysis
2.intro:
Broad histone marks (H3K27me3, H3K36me3, H3K9me3) spread over kilobases rather
than sharp peaks, so a window-based test catches diffuse changes that peak-based
DiffBind can miss. This notebook counts reads in sliding windows with csaw, filters
background windows, normalizes for composition bias, fits a quasi-likelihood model and
combines window tests into region-level FDR.

csaw has no osx-arm64 bioconda build: on Apple Silicon this route reports a gap and
falls back to DiffBind. Run on linux-x64 / darwin-x64 for the window analysis. A user
GTF/GFF3 annotates the differential regions.

3.title: CUT&Tag — DiffBind + edgeR
3.intro:
CUT&Tag profiles protein-DNA interactions with very low background, so FRiP is
typically high and fewer reads are needed. The downstream statistics match ChIP: a
consensus peakset, read counting, and differential binding. This preset uses edgeR
(often more sensitive with few replicates) instead of DESeq2.

CUT&Tag peak calling (SEACR) has no nf-core wrapper yet — pass the SEACR peaks in
directly via the sample sheet's Peaks column. The rest of the route is identical to
ChIP, which is why one plugin covers both.

4.title: Consensus peakset only
4.intro:
Build a reproducible consensus peakset from called peaks without differential
analysis: import per-sample peaks, remove blacklist regions, keep sites present in at
least min_occupancy samples, and visualise overlap with an UpSet plot. Useful for
defining a region universe before counting, or for a quick reproducibility check.

5.title: Annotation only
5.intro:
Annotate called peaks to genomic features with ChIPseeker: promoter/exon/intron/
intergenic distribution, nearest gene, distance to TSS, plus a TSS coverage profile and
peak heatmap. Requires a user GTF/GFF3 (or prebuilt TxDb) — the plugin bundles no
target-genome annotation. Gene symbols additionally need a user org.db.

6.title: Count matrix exploration
6.intro:
Start from an existing peak x sample count matrix (featureCounts or a DiffBind
export) rather than BAMs: normalize for library size, run sample PCA to see whether
condition or batch dominates, and save the normalized table. A fast exploratory pass
when counting already happened upstream.
